exposure: Parents' experiences with mode of birth for preterm singleton pregnancies
Knowledge about maternal and infant risks of different modes of preterm birth
Communication preferences with respect to mode of birth
Discussion of mode of birth prior to birth
Perceived choice regarding mode of birth
Receipt of written information about mode of birth
outcome: Reported experiences regarding mode of birth
Levels of knowledge about maternal and infant risks of preterm birth modes
Expressed communication preferences for counselling on mode of birth
Proportion of parents given a choice about mode of birth
Proportion of parents unaware of maternal risks for cesarean delivery
cohort: An online survey of 153 Canadian parents (152 mothers) who had experienced the preterm birth of a live-born infant between 2010 and 2019.
finding: Few Canadian parents reported receiving a choice about mode of preterm birth, being aware of associated risks, or receiving written information, highlighting an urgent need for better informational tools.
mod_finding: A minority of parents (20.8%-36.4% depending on gestational age) reported being given a choice about mode of birth, and 39.6% of women who had a cesarean delivery were unaware of the maternal risks.
cross-section timing: Data collected from August to September 2019
gest_age: Extremely preterm (<28 weeks), very preterm (28-31 weeks), and moderate-to-late preterm (32-36 weeks)
